surprises.head: Jacob Fowler stole one
surprises.body: Fowler allowed 1 goal on 34 shots, worth 3.9 expected goals: 2.9 fewer than expected. That is more than Montréal’s winning margin. Starting goalies have a night this good about once every 60 starts.

surprises.head: Montréal brought the hits
surprises.body: Montréal’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 170, against their usual 98 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 40 games.

story.head: Fowler stands on his head against the Jets
paras: Lane Hutson and Kaiden Guhle scored less than four minutes apart early in the second to put the Canadiens up 2-0. Isak Rosén cut Montréal’s lead to 2-1 with less than five minutes left.

The Canadiens were outshot 34-21, but their looks were better, and the chances came out about even. Jacob Fowler made 33 saves for the Habs, and Stuart Skinner kept the Jets in it, stopping 19 of 21. Fowler has won five straight starts.
The Canadiens killed all four Jets power plays. The Canadiens improved to 6-3-2, fifth in the Atlantic, while the Jets fell to 4-4-3, slipping to seventh in the Central.

items.text: The Jets are winless in five (0-3-2).
Gabriel Vilardi extended his point streak against Montréal to six games.
Isak Rosén scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 14 (eleven games played since).
With Nick Suzuki out, Oliver Kapanen took his spot, though he won only 4 of 12 faceoffs.
